note: Written for Drivly in plain language. Do not copy text from commercial DTC sites.

strings.manufacturerMeaning: Your car maker defines this code. Its exact meaning depends on the brand and model.
strings.categoryMeaning: We don't have a detailed explanation for this code yet. From its number, it belongs to: {category}.
strings.fallbackAction: Ask a garage to check it, or search online for this code together with your car model.
strings.idle: Speed, idle or cruise control problem

P0300.title: Engine misfire, several cylinders
P0300.meaning: The engine isn't burning fuel properly in more than one cylinder, so it runs unevenly.
P0300.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0301.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 1
P0301.meaning: Cylinder 1 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0301.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0302.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 2
P0302.meaning: Cylinder 2 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0302.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0303.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 3
P0303.meaning: Cylinder 3 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0303.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0304.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 4
P0304.meaning: Cylinder 4 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0304.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0305.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 5
P0305.meaning: Cylinder 5 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0305.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0306.title: Engine misfire, cylinder 6
P0306.meaning: Cylinder 6 isn't burning fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
P0306.safeToDrive: Short trips, gently. If the engine light flashes, stop: unburned fuel can damage the catalytic converter.

P0171.title: Engine running lean (bank 1)
P0171.meaning: The engine is getting too much air or too little fuel, so the computer is adding fuel to compensate.
P0171.safeToDrive: Yes, for now. Get it checked within a few weeks.
causes: Weak fuel pump or clogged filter
P0171.action: Ask a garage to check for air leaks and the air flow sensor.

P0174.title: Engine running lean (bank 2)
P0174.meaning: The engine is getting too much air or too little fuel on its second cylinder bank.
P0174.safeToDrive: Yes, for now. Get it checked within a few weeks.
P0174.action: Ask a garage to check for air leaks.

P0172.title: Engine running rich (bank 1)
P0172.meaning: The engine is getting too much fuel, which wastes fuel and can foul spark plugs.
P0172.safeToDrive: Yes, for now. Get it checked soon.
P0172.action: Ask a garage to check the injectors and sensors.

P0175.title: Engine running rich (bank 2)
P0175.meaning: The engine is getting too much fuel on its second cylinder bank.
P0175.safeToDrive: Yes, for now. Get it checked soon.
P0175.action: Ask a garage to check the injectors and sensors.

P0420.title: Catalytic converter less efficient (bank 1)
P0420.technicalTitle: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold, bank 1
P0420.meaning: The part that cleans the exhaust isn't working as well as it should.
P0420.action: Have it checked before your next inspection.

P0430.title: Catalytic converter less efficient (bank 2)
P0430.technicalTitle: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold, bank 2
P0430.meaning: The exhaust cleaner on the second bank isn't working as well as it should.
P0430.action: Have it checked before your next inspection.

P0128.title: Engine warms up too slowly
P0128.technicalTitle: Coolant temperature below thermostat regulating temperature
P0128.meaning: The engine takes too long to reach its normal temperature, usually because the thermostat stays open.
P0128.action: Ask a garage to replace the thermostat.

P0217.title: Engine overheating
P0217.meaning: The engine got hotter than it should. Overheating can seriously damage the engine.
P0217.safeToDrive: No. Stop safely, turn the engine off and let it cool. Don't open the coolant cap while hot.
P0217.action: Check the coolant level once cold, then get it to a garage.

P0117.title: Engine temperature sensor reads too low
P0117.technicalTitle: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit low
P0117.meaning: The engine temperature sensor is sending a signal that's too low to be real.
symptoms: Fan may run all the time
P0117.safeToDrive: Yes, carefully: the car may not know its real temperature.
P0117.action: Have the sensor and its wiring checked.

P0118.title: Engine temperature sensor reads too high
P0118.technicalTitle: Engine coolant temperature sensor circuit high
P0118.meaning: The engine temperature sensor is sending a signal that's too high to be real.
symptoms: Fan may run all the time
P0118.action: Have the sensor and its wiring checked.

P0101.title: Air flow sensor reading off
P0101.technicalTitle: Mass air flow sensor circuit range/performance
P0101.meaning: The sensor that measures air going into the engine gives values that don't make sense.
P0101.action: Ask a garage to clean or test the air flow sensor.

P0102.title: Air flow sensor signal too low
P0102.technicalTitle: Mass air flow sensor circuit low
P0102.meaning: The air flow sensor signal is too low.

P0113.title: Intake air temperature sensor reads too high
P0113.technicalTitle: Intake air temperature sensor circuit high
P0113.meaning: The intake air temperature sensor signal is out of range.

P0130.title: Oxygen sensor problem (front, bank 1)
P0130.meaning: The front oxygen sensor, which helps the engine mix fuel and air, isn't working right.

P0133.title: Oxygen sensor slow to respond
P0133.technicalTitle: O2 sensor circuit slow response, bank 1 sensor 1
P0133.meaning: The front oxygen sensor reacts too slowly, so the engine can't fine-tune its fuel mixture.
P0133.safeToDrive: Yes, for now. Get it checked within a few weeks.
P0133.action: Check soon: the sensor usually needs replacing.

P0135.title: Oxygen sensor heater problem (front)
P0135.technicalTitle: O2 sensor heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 1
P0135.meaning: The front oxygen sensor's heater doesn't work, so the sensor takes longer to start working after a cold start.
symptoms: Higher fuel use just after starting

P0136.title: Oxygen sensor problem (rear, bank 1)
P0136.meaning: The rear oxygen sensor, which checks the catalytic converter, isn't working right.
P0136.action: Have it checked before your next inspection.

P0141.title: Oxygen sensor heater problem (rear)
P0141.technicalTitle: O2 sensor heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 2
P0141.meaning: The rear oxygen sensor's heater doesn't work.

P0011.title: Camshaft timing off (bank 1)
P0011.technicalTitle: Intake camshaft position timing over-advanced or system performance, bank 1
P0011.meaning: The variable valve timing isn't reaching the position the engine asks for.
P0011.action: Check the oil level first, then see a garage.

P0016.title: Crankshaft and camshaft out of sync
P0016.technicalTitle: Crankshaft/camshaft position correlation, bank 1 sensor A
P0016.meaning: The engine's crankshaft and camshaft aren't lined up as expected. Often a stretched timing chain or a slipped belt.
P0016.safeToDrive: Drive as little as possible: a failing timing chain or belt can destroy the engine.

P0087.title: Fuel pressure too low
P0087.meaning: The fuel system can't keep enough pressure to feed the engine properly.
P0087.safeToDrive: Carefully: the engine may lose power suddenly.

P0093.title: Large fuel leak detected
P0093.meaning: The car detected a big drop in fuel pressure, which can mean fuel is leaking.
P0093.safeToDrive: No if you smell fuel: fire risk. Stop and call for help.
P0093.action: Stop if you smell fuel, and have the car towed.

P0234.title: Turbo pressure too high
P0234.meaning: The turbo is producing more boost than the engine allows.
P0234.action: Have the turbo controls checked soon.

P0299.title: Turbo pressure too low
P0299.meaning: The turbo isn't producing as much boost as expected.
P0299.action: Ask a garage to check the turbo hoses first.

P0325.title: Knock sensor problem
P0325.meaning: The sensor that listens for engine knock isn't working, so the engine protects itself by reducing power.

P0335.title: Crankshaft sensor problem
P0335.meaning: The engine computer can't read the crankshaft position, which it needs to run the engine.
P0335.safeToDrive: Risky: the engine may stall without warning.

P0340.title: Camshaft sensor problem
P0340.technicalTitle: Camshaft position sensor A circuit, bank 1
P0340.meaning: The engine computer can't read the camshaft position.

P0380.title: Glow plug circuit problem
P0380.meaning: A diesel glow plug circuit isn't working, which makes cold starts harder.

P0401.title: Exhaust recirculation flow too low
P0401.meaning: Not enough exhaust gas is being fed back into the engine to reduce emissions.
P0401.action: Have the EGR valve cleaned or replaced.

P0402.title: Exhaust recirculation flow too high
P0402.meaning: Too much exhaust gas is being fed back into the engine.

P0440.title: Fuel vapor system problem
P0440.meaning: The system that traps fuel vapors from the tank has a problem.

P0441.title: Fuel vapor purge flow incorrect
P0441.technicalTitle: Evaporative emission system incorrect purge flow
P0441.meaning: The system that burns stored fuel vapors isn't flowing as expected.

P0442.title: Small fuel vapor leak
P0442.technicalTitle: Evaporative emission system leak detected (small leak)
P0442.meaning: The system that traps fuel vapors from the tank has a small leak.
causes: Fuel cap not tight or worn seal
P0442.action: Tighten the fuel cap until it clicks. If it comes back, have the hoses checked.

P0455.title: Large fuel vapor leak
P0455.technicalTitle: Evaporative emission system leak detected (large leak)
P0455.meaning: The fuel vapor system has a large leak, often a missing or loose fuel cap.

P0456.title: Very small fuel vapor leak
P0456.technicalTitle: Evaporative emission system leak detected (very small leak)
P0456.meaning: A tiny leak in the fuel vapor system.
P0456.action: Replace the fuel cap if it's old.

P0500.title: Vehicle speed sensor problem
P0500.meaning: The car can't read its speed correctly.
P0500.safeToDrive: Yes, carefully: some assist systems may not work.

P0505.title: Idle control problem
P0505.meaning: The engine can't hold a steady idle speed.
symptoms: Idle too high or too low
P0505.action: Ask a garage to clean the throttle body.

P0506.title: Idle speed lower than expected
P0506.technicalTitle: Idle control system RPM lower than expected
P0506.meaning: The engine idles slower than it should.

P0507.title: Idle speed higher than expected
P0507.technicalTitle: Idle control system RPM higher than expected
P0507.meaning: The engine idles faster than it should.

P0520.title: Oil pressure sensor problem
P0520.meaning: The car can't read the engine oil pressure reliably.
P0520.safeToDrive: Check the oil level first. If the oil light stays on, stop.
P0520.action: Check the oil level and get it checked soon.

P0524.title: Oil pressure too low
P0524.meaning: The engine doesn't have enough oil pressure. Running like this can destroy the engine within minutes.
P0524.safeToDrive: No. Stop safely and turn the engine off.
P0524.action: Stop, check the oil level and call for help.

P0562.title: System voltage low
P0562.meaning: The car's electrical voltage is lower than it should be.
P0562.safeToDrive: Yes, but the car may not restart.
P0562.action: Have the battery and alternator tested.

P0563.title: System voltage high
P0563.meaning: The car's electrical voltage is too high, which can damage electronics.
P0563.action: Have the charging system checked soon.

P0571.title: Brake switch problem
P0571.meaning: The car can't read the brake pedal switch correctly.
P0571.safeToDrive: Check your brake lights work. If not, don't drive until fixed.

P0606.title: Engine computer problem
P0606.meaning: The engine computer found a fault in itself.
P0606.safeToDrive: Carefully: the engine may behave unpredictably.

P0700.title: Transmission problem reported
P0700.meaning: The gearbox computer has stored its own fault code.
causes: See the gearbox computer for details
P0700.action: A garage needs to read the gearbox computer.

P0715.title: Gearbox speed sensor problem
P0715.meaning: The automatic gearbox can't read its input speed.

P0730.title: Wrong gear ratio
P0730.meaning: The gearbox isn't in the gear it should be, or is slipping.
P0730.action: Have the gearbox fluid and solenoids checked.

P2002.title: Diesel particulate filter less efficient
P2002.technicalTitle: Diesel particulate filter efficiency below threshold, bank 1
P2002.meaning: The filter that catches soot from diesel exhaust isn't working as well as it should.

P2463.title: Diesel particulate filter clogged
P2463.meaning: The diesel particulate filter is too full of soot.
P2463.safeToDrive: A long drive at steady motorway speed can help it clean itself. If it doesn't, see a garage.
P2463.action: Try a 20-minute motorway drive, then re-check.

P242F.title: Diesel particulate filter ash full
P242F.technicalTitle: Diesel particulate filter restriction, ash accumulation
P242F.meaning: The particulate filter is filled with ash that can't be burned off.
P242F.action: The filter needs cleaning or replacing.

U0100.title: Lost communication with engine computer
U0100.meaning: Another computer in the car can't talk to the engine computer.
U0100.action: Check the battery, then get it checked today.

U0121.title: Lost communication with ABS
U0121.technicalTitle: Lost communication with anti-lock brake system module
U0121.meaning: The car can't talk to the anti-lock brake computer, so ABS may not work.
U0121.safeToDrive: Normal brakes work, but without ABS. Drive carefully.

U0073.title: Car network problem
U0073.technicalTitle: Control module communication bus A off
U0073.meaning: The network that connects the car's computers has a problem.

C0035.title: Front-left wheel speed sensor
C0035.technicalTitle: Left front wheel speed sensor circuit
C0035.meaning: The ABS can't read the front-left wheel's speed.
C0035.safeToDrive: Normal brakes work, but without ABS. Drive carefully.
